evidence: physical_forward_model(keep): completion_time_h 36.96, thermal_warning false, min critical margin +0.479 C, min capacity margin 0.623 kg/h
physical_forward_model(warm): 39.72 h, no warnings; physical_forward_model(moderate): 50.46 h; physical_forward_model(cool): 68.27 h — all slower than KEEP
Observations 0–6 h: product temp -43.4→-37.1 C (critical -28 C, ample margin), pressure stable ~8.0 Pa, ice 0.00222→0.00194 kg/vial, no past excursions
Model warnings: reconstruction only, quasi-steady representative vial, sampled constraint onset; unknowns include thermometry bias and receiving capacity curve
submission.rationale: Forward-model trajectories for all four allowed schedules show KEEP (shelf -31.4 C → -20 C at 8 h, 8 Pa) completes primary drying fastest at ~36.96 h absolute elapsed, with minimum critical-temperature margin +0.48 C (no excursion past -28 C) and minimum vapor-capacity margin ~0.62 kg/h (peak sublimation ~0.51 kg/h vs 1.14 kg/h capacity). Counterintuitively, warmer shelf steps are predicted slower: at 8 Pa the process is mass-transfer/vapor-flow limited, so added heat lowers margin without increasing sublimation throughput. No past thermal or capacity excursion is evident in observations (product stayed ≤ -37 C through 6 h, pressure ~8 Pa). Therefore KEEP is both the forecast schedule and the highest-throughput feasible action.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is a calibrated quasi-steady reconstruction (kv_scale 1.08, rp_scale 1.39, residual RMS 0.72) from only 6 h of synthetic early thermometry/mass data; late-cycle Kv/Rp shifts, thermometry bias (weighted lump interface channel, not bottom thermometry), and the receiving equipment's true pressure-dependent vapor-capacity curve (listed as missing parameters) could change completion time by several hours and could produce thermal excursions in edge-vial or lower-Kv populations not captured by the representative-vial model. The thin +0.48 C thermal margin under KEEP means model error, not just the schedule choice, governs whether the critical temperature is approached late in drying.

Observations at 0–6 h: product temp rose -43.4→-37.1°C, ice 0.00222→0.001936 kg/vial, pressure stable ~8.0 Pa, consistent with model trajectory (no measured pressure mismatch)
Calibration: kv_scale=1.154, rp_scale=1.346, residual RMS 0.514 (nfev 9) — margin uncertainty exceeds 0.018°C
submission.rationale: KEEP schedule forecasts 37.1 h completion with no capacity warning (min capacity margin ~0.59 kg/h against 1.14 kg/h limit) and no nominal thermal warning, but its minimum critical margin is only 0.018°C at Tcrit=-28°C. Given calibration residual RMS 0.51, Kv RSD 0.11, approximate population factors, and unknown receiving heat/resistance shifts and possible thermometry bias, KEEP's margin is within noise and a real excursion risk — and any excursion invalidates the whole batch. WARM (-22°C shelf) costs only ~2.8 h more (39.9 h) with ~1.05°C margin and no capacity or thermal warnings; MODERATE (-26°C) is slower (50.7 h) and dominated since the KEEP plan itself steps to -20°C at 8h. Warm is therefore the highest-throughput action with a defensible safety margin under model uncertainty.
submission.uncertainty: Completion time and margins come from an experimental, unqualified lumped population model calibrated on only 6 h of early thermography/mass data (kv_scale 1.15, rp_scale 1.35, residual RMS 0.51); true Kv/Rp in the receiving equipment, condenser deposition-rate behavior, pressure-dependent vapor capacity, shared utility headroom, and possible thermometry bias are unknown. Thermal margin extrema are solver-mesh samples, not certified continuous extrema. KEEP's 0.018°C margin could realistically be negative; warm's 1.05°C margin could also be eroded. Completion forecast uncertainty estimated at roughly ±4-6 h.
